tools.bunkershot3d_workbench.title: BunkerShot3D designer workbench (W2 sole parameters, W3 sand condition, F0 dynamic-RFT shot, W7 metrics, playability window, bounce utilisation, animated sole load field, 3-D shot animation through the ADR-0027 viewport, linked scalar traces with a validity band, F1 sand-field cross-sections, A/B comparison, validity verdict)
tools.bunkershot3d_workbench.notes: Moved out of engines.load_and_simulate by #8618: the tile is a club-design workbench, not an engine load/simulate surface, and the two launcher tiles (bunkershot3d -> a notebook script, bunker_shot -> the GUI) were reconciled into this one entry point. The computation lives in src/tools/bunker_shot_gui/model.py, which imports no GUI toolkit and is the layer a React port would consume; the v1 API route (#9545) serves a bounded nominal solve from it, and no web page exists yet. The visualization suite (epic #8699) keeps that split: shot3d.py and traces.py compute, render3d.py and render_traces.py draw headlessly through matplotlib, and viewport_widgets.py only wires them to a canvas. A React port would consume shot3d.viewport_payload, which is the backend-neutral ADR-0027 ViewportOverlayPayload and carries the envelope status and fidelity tier in its metadata so any renderer can stamp its own frames. The F1 sand cut (#8710, #8711) keeps the same split and adds one constraint a port must honour: the field carries its fidelity tier and validity status as data covered by a SHA-256 over the provenance and the arrays together, so any client that renders a field must read the standing out of the file rather than out of its filename, and must refuse a field whose digest does not match.

tools.capture_rig.title: Capture Rig camera controller with the live view as the central pane and every control in a movable dock (step rail with the next action, settings tabs, action grid, log drawer) with saved layouts, themed header with status strip and workflow-grouped actions that reflow to fit a narrow pane, transport-style recorder (countdown, presets, REC readout, live view during the take), overlay player, camera-subset matching (variants), model-on-video overlays, provenance viewer and manual point annotation/editing; layout model with named layout presets, an interactive layout editor, live preview and playback composited through the chosen multiview layout, and composite multiview video export; non-destructive swing trim/crop and separate video export, visible capture library with durable swing notes, import/open/edit, archive/restore and storage management; saved coaching lines/arrows/circles/ellipses/rectangles with selection, resize, undo/redo, frame visibility and annotated still/video exports; reference comparison and overlay player force/torque vector arrow layers (FTO-25, #11310)
tools.capture_rig.reason: Drives local USB cameras through ffmpeg/DirectShow and reads multi-gigabyte recordings from disk (#9619); variants, overlays, provenance and annotation (#9790, #9791) and the multiview layout model/presets/editor and the layout-composited live preview and playback (#9810, #9811, #9812, #9813, #9814) run on the same local session trees; desktop-only candidate pending #7460.
tools.capture_rig.notes: Editing/library #9860/#9861 run in the native capture app. Saved selections preserve original media, pixel coordinates and frame clocks; exports carry source hashes and edit provenance. Coaching drawings #9862 provide native saved shape references, undo/redo, source-frame visibility and annotated still/video export. Expert reference imports #9864 add a native library and explicit C3D/CIR/body-target mappings; 2D video references remain distinct. Camera registration, synchronized overlays and expert alignment controls shipped through #9896. Capture journey #9913 adds persistent swing identity, saved per-capture action outcomes, detector/edit associations, linked workflow help and provenance, and Qt pop-out/redock/fullscreen controls. My Clubs #9905 adds native catalog/custom equipment editing, unit-aware partial measurements, archive/restore, capture assignment and immutable equipment context in fit reports; current body models apply no club constraints. Common-reference calibration #9898/#9900 adds capture-owned paper/ruler observations, original-frame point editing, repeated placements, asynchronous canonical camera estimation, reviewable result history and shared native/generated help; lens profiles remain required. Guided cross-capture reuse requires explicit optics/scene confirmation, retains portable original evidence and revalidates it before processing. Physical accuracy and packaged-runtime qualification remain pending under #9897. Model-only analysis and Draw on Comparison reuse the coaching editor, appearance, club/ellipsoid/handedness controls and scene-bound metric planes/points. Comparison drawing PNGs preserve original pixels; video applies the saved crop. Shared metric readouts and Trace v2 marker/club imports use the same controls (#9942). Native Camera Setup #9952 adds background ELP discovery, named views, mode selection, connection checks and versioned plans linked from the wizard. Reference comparison and capture-rig overlay player render calibrated force and torque vector layers on source footage with sidecar receipts and provenance (FTO-25, #11310). These desktop routes do not establish web parity.
